Lessons.Title: Which Variable to Solve for? (Part 1)
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning objective: isolate an indicated quantity in a multi-variable equation and explain why that form is useful for area, cost and shared-work contexts. Edulytiks original adaptation based on Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 2 Lesson 8, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/2/8/preparation.html (CC BY 4.0). Addressing HSA-CED.A.4 and HSA-REI.B.3; Building Towards HSA-CED.A.4.

Original geometric task: parallelogram area A=bh, where base b>0 and height h>0. Isolate h=A/b when area and base are known, or b=A/h when area and height are known. For A=52.5 square centimetres and b=7.5 centimetres, h=7 cm. Check 7.5×7=52.5. Variable isolation is more efficient than repeatedly guessing a height.

Original division context: 3.6 km of trail is divided into equal maintenance stretches for n positive-integer volunteers. Each receives length l=3.6/n km. To find number of volunteers from assigned length, rearrange n=3.6/l, with l>0 and n an integer, and check whether computed n is valid before interpreting.

Student task: read equations, identify which variable a question asks for, isolate it using reversible moves and substitute at least two valid inputs. Include a sensible unit and domain for every variable. Teacher-scored rubric (0–2 each, max 8): correct target, valid isolation, correct verification with units and coherent contextual explanation. One formula alone does not establish modeling understanding.

KeyConcepts.Title: Isolate variable
KeyConcepts.Definition: Rearrange an equation so one chosen symbol is alone on one side.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use inverse operations and state nonzero divisors.

KeyConcepts.Title: Domain in division
KeyConcepts.Definition: Rewriting with a denominator introduces a nonzero requirement.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Check a zero divisor never enters the permitted context.
KeyConcepts.Example: With positive base length b, h=A/b is well-defined.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equivalent forms by use
KeyConcepts.Definition: Different forms of one relation highlight different unknowns.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Choose the form matching the requested output.

WorkedExamples.Title: Solve for height
WorkedExamples.Question: A parallelogram has A=52.5 cm² and b=7.5 cm. Find h.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use equivalence-preserving algebra, show domain restrictions and independently check a test value.
Steps: Divide by nonzero base b to isolate h=A/b.
WorkedExamples.Check: Area is base times perpendicular height.

WorkedExamples.Title: Solve for volunteer count
WorkedExamples.Question: A 3.6 km trail is divided equally, each stretch l=0.45 km. Find n.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use equivalence-preserving algebra, show domain restrictions and independently check a test value.
Steps: Divide by nonzero l to get n=3.6/l.
WorkedExamples.Check: Positive whole number and total length satisfy context.

WorkedExamples.Title: Compare two useful rearrangements
WorkedExamples.Question: From a rectangular perimeter P=2L+2W, solve for L.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use equivalence-preserving algebra, show domain restrictions and independently check a test value.
WorkedExamples.Answer: L=P/2−W, giving L=10 for this example.
WorkedExamples.Check: The perimeter formula holds after substitution.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Dividing by zero when isolating a variable
Ignoring integer restrictions after solving a real equation
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Fractional volunteer counts are impossible here.

SummaryPoints: Solve for the quantity needed before substituting values.
A=bh gives h=A/b for positive b.
nl=3.6 gives n=3.6/l for positive l; contextual n must be a positive integer.
Teacher reviews variable choice, units and why the form is useful.
